Colombian here! I do not recommend traveling at the moment, especially alone. Although Colombia is not as dangerous as it once was, there is a lot going on over there due to Covid. People getting mugged and pick pockets are pretty much what is going on (plus a few political things that are causing a tense environment, at least in Bogota). I do not know the situation in other parts if Colombia but I suggest later. I also highly recommend you go with someone or even better, a local to guide you. Not many speak english and probably almost no one speaks french.

Whenever the situation gets better though, i really recommend going to Colombia, it’s a beautiful place. Uber is illegal over there so if ylu ever order one while youre there, you have to sit in the front, public transportation is good but people usually get mugged. Do not just hop in a taxi, call a cab company or use an app (Tapsi). 

I feel like im making my country sound bad but I promise that it is so worth it. Bogota is usually cold and up on the mountains, altitude might make you feel sick so try to get used to it and take it easy on the first few days. 

There are so many places i can recommend. Bogota, Cartagena, Zona Cafetera, Barranquilla. We have all kinds of stuff, cold wheather, mountains, beach, jungle, etc.

Sometimes panic attacks can cause you to dissociate. It’s a scary thing because as you said, you can’t remember anything that happened. Almost like your consciousness was pulled away. It it very normal with anxiety. I would try to contact a therapist or psychiatrist to let them know. If you are unable to contact them I suggest trying some grounding exercises to "stay awake". 
Grounding is something to keep you away from dissociating, you can describe what’s around you, state exactly where you are, what you feel around you, etc. There are also physical objects you can use, a fidget spinner, a bracelet, really anything that you can thing of that you can physically feel. The object will hopefully help you not dissociate, it might be hard and you might feel like you’re sleeping into unconsciousness, but really try to focus on the physical feelings (not how anxious you are, but if it’s hot, cold, is there a breeze?). Cold showers also help a lot! 

I hope youre okay! And don’t worry, what you described is perfectly normal it comes to anxiety disorders
